edges.description: UV exposure raises melanoma risk on the genetically susceptible (p16-deficient) background, modifying penetrance rather than initiating the germline lesion.

edges.source: Brain Imaging Surveillance for p14ARF Carriers

nodes.description: Astrocytic nervous-system tumors are the characteristic neural component that defines this syndrome relative to CDKN2A familial melanoma without neural tumors. Brain neoplasms as a group occurred in roughly 29-33% of ascertained cases.

evidence.reference_title: A germline deletion of p14(ARF) but not CDKN2A in a melanoma-neural system tumour syndrome family.
evidence.snippet: The melanoma-astrocytoma syndrome is characterized by a dual predisposition to melanoma and neural system tumours, commonly astrocytoma.

evidence.reference_title: A familial syndrome with cutaneous malignant melanoma and cerebral astrocytoma.
evidence.snippet: In two patients with both malignant melanoma and astrocytoma, the brain tumor followed the diagnosis of melanoma by a period of 2 and 10 years and was the primary cause of morbidity and mortality.

nodes.description: Avoidance of ultraviolet light, particularly sunburns and tanning booths, to reduce the environmental contribution to melanoma risk in genetically susceptible skin. Tobacco use is also to be avoided.

evidence.reference_title: CDKN2A Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: Agents/circumstances to avoid: Ultraviolet light exposure, particularly sunburns and tanning booths; tobacco use.

nodes.description: Full-body and brain MRI is recommended specifically for carriers of a CDKN2A variant affecting the p14ARF isoform who have a family history of nervous-system tumors, which is the surveillance arm that distinguishes this syndrome from melanoma-only CDKN2A families.
nodes.id: Brain Imaging Surveillance for p14ARF Carriers

evidence.reference_title: CDKN2A Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: full-body and brain MRI in those with a CDKN2A pathogenic variant affecting the p14ARF isoform in the setting of a family history of nervous system tumors.

meta.association: Germline alterations of the CDKN2A locus (encoding p16INK4A and p14ARF) cause melanoma and neural system tumor syndrome; the neural tumor component has been associated particularly with lesions affecting p14ARF.

evidence.reference_title: Germ-line deletion involving the INK4 locus in familial proneness to melanoma and nervous system tumors.
evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that multiple cancer susceptibility in these two families ensues from contiguous tumor suppressor gene deletion.

evidence.reference_title: A germline deletion of p14(ARF) but not CDKN2A in a melanoma-neural system tumour syndrome family.
evidence.snippet: We describe a family characterized by multiple melanoma and neural cell tumours segregating with a germline deletion of the p14(ARF)-specific exon 1beta of the CDKN2A gene.

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive analysis of CDKN2A (p16INK4A/p14ARF) and CDKN2B genes in 53 melanoma index cases considered to be at heightened risk of melanoma.
evidence.snippet: we identified a p14ARF exon 1beta missense germline mutation (G16D) in a melanoma-neural system tumour syndrome (CMM+NST) family

nodes.description: Cutaneous malignant melanoma, often as multiple primaries, as in CDKN2A-related familial melanoma. In genomic-ascertained melanoma-astrocytoma cohorts it was seen in roughly 17-29% of cases.

evidence.reference_title: A familial syndrome with cutaneous malignant melanoma and cerebral astrocytoma.
evidence.snippet: We describe a family in which cutaneous malignant melanoma or cerebral astrocytoma, or both, developed in eight members over three generations.

evidence.reference_title: Estimated Prevalence, Tumor Spectrum, and Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Like Phenotype of CDKN2A-Related Melanoma-Astrocytoma Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: while cutaneous melanoma (2 of 12, 17%) and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (2 of 12, 17%) were the most common nonneural malignant neoplasms

nodes.description: Cutaneous neurofibromas are common in MAS case series and can lead to a clinical misdiagnosis of neurofibromatosis type 1.

evidence.reference_title: Estimated Prevalence, Tumor Spectrum, and Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Like Phenotype of CDKN2A-Related Melanoma-Astrocytoma Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Cutaneous neurofibromas (7 of 14, 50%) and schwannomas (2 of 14, 14%) were also common.

nodes.description: Unopposed MDM2 ubiquitinates p53 and targets it for proteasomal degradation, lowering p53 levels and activity.

evidence.reference_title: Regulatory Network of ARF in Cancer Development.
evidence.snippet: As a factor that induces senescence, the role of ARF as a tumor suppressor is closely linked to the p53-MDM2 axis, which is a key process that restrains tumor formation.

nodes.description: With the RB and p53 brakes disabled, melanocytes and glial/astrocytic cells bypass cellular senescence and expand clonally, accumulating further somatic hits toward malignancy.
nodes.id: Escape from Cellular Senescence and Clonal Expansion

evidence.reference_title: Genome-Wide Overexpression Screen Identifies Genes Able to Bypass p16-Mediated Senescence in Melanoma.
evidence.snippet: Malignant melanomas often arise from nevi, which result from initial oncogene-induced hyperproliferation of melanocytes that are maintained in a CDKN2A/p16-mediated senescent state.

evidence.reference_title: The p16INK4a-RB pathway: molecular link between cellular senescence and tumor suppression.
evidence.snippet: In contrast to normal cells, the function of the p16INK4a gene or its downstream mediators is frequently deregulated in many types of human cancers, illustrating the importance of cellular senescence in tumor suppression.

nodes.description: The constitutional first hit: a germline alteration of the CDKN2A locus at 9p21, classically a deletion spanning the INK4 gene cluster, or a lesion restricted to the p14ARF-specific exon 1beta. Because the locus's tumor-suppressor products are encoded in overlapping reading frames, a single structural lesion can inactivate more than one.

evidence.reference_title: Germ-line deletion involving the INK4 locus in familial proneness to melanoma and nervous system tumors.
evidence.snippet: In the family segregating the melanoma/NST syndrome, a large germ-line deletion ablated the whole p16, p19, and p15 gene cluster (or INK4 locus)

evidence.reference_title: A germline deletion of p14(ARF) but not CDKN2A in a melanoma-neural system tumour syndrome family.
evidence.snippet: We describe a family characterized by multiple melanoma and neural cell tumours segregating with a germline deletion of the p14(ARF)-specific exon 1beta of the CDKN2A gene.

genetic_context.description: Heterozygous germline deletions at CDKN2A; the neural-tumor component is associated particularly with lesions that remove or disrupt p14ARF.

nodes.description: High-grade astrocytic tumors, including glioblastoma, are among the brain neoplasms seen in affected individuals.

evidence.reference_title: Estimated Prevalence, Tumor Spectrum, and Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Like Phenotype of CDKN2A-Related Melanoma-Astrocytoma Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: brain neoplasms (4 of 12, 33%; 1 glioblastoma, 1 gliosarcoma, 1 astrocytoma, 1 unspecified type) and schwannomas (3 of 12, 25%) were the most common malignant and benign neural tumors

nodes.description: Reduced p53 activity blunts the apoptotic and senescence responses to oncogenic and genotoxic stress, a defect thought to underlie the nervous-system (astrocytic/glioma) tumor component of the syndrome.

biological_processes: signal transduction in response to DNA damage

evidence.reference_title: Beyond effector caspase inhibition: Bcl2L12 neutralizes p53 signaling in glioblastoma.
evidence.snippet: The prime importance of p53 signaling for gliomapathogenesis is further evidenced by epistatic genetic events targeting additional pathway components including deletion of p14 (Arf) (CDKN2A) and amplification of the p53-degrading ubiquitin ligases MDM2 and MDM4.

nodes.description: p14ARF (the alternate reading frame product of the CDKN2A locus) sequesters and inhibits MDM2. A germline lesion restricted to p14ARF (including exon 1beta deletions and the G16D missense) can be the critical abnormality for the neural-tumor component of this syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: A germline deletion of p14(ARF) but not CDKN2A in a melanoma-neural system tumour syndrome family.
evidence.snippet: Our results are consistent with either: (i) loss of p14(ARF) function being the critical abnormality associated with this syndrome, rather than contiguous loss of both the CDKN2A and CDKN2B genes as suggested previously

evidence.reference_title: CDKN2A exon 1B deletion predisposing to melanoma and neural system tumour syndrome.
evidence.snippet: families with mutations involving the p14ARF-specific exon 1B may be predisposed to central nervous system tumours.

evidence.reference_title: INK4a/ARF: a multifunctional tumor suppressor locus.
evidence.snippet: The INK4a/ARF locus encodes two physically linked tumor suppressor proteins, p16(INK4a) and ARF, which regulate the RB and p53 pathways, respectively.

nodes.description: p16INK4A is a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor that binds CDK4 and CDK6 and blocks their association with cyclin D. Loss of p16INK4A removes this inhibition and de-represses the RB pathway.

evidence.reference_title: The p16INK4a-RB pathway: molecular link between cellular senescence and tumor suppression.
evidence.snippet: The p16INK4a tumor suppressor protein functions as an inhibitor of CDK4 and CDK6, the D-type cyclin-dependent kinases that initiate the phosphorylation of the retinoblastoma tumor suppressor protein, RB.

evidence.reference_title: INK4a/ARF: a multifunctional tumor suppressor locus.
evidence.snippet: The INK4a/ARF locus encodes two physically linked tumor suppressor proteins, p16(INK4a) and ARF, which regulate the RB and p53 pathways, respectively.

nodes.description: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor is among the neural cancers reported in MAS case series.

evidence.reference_title: Estimated Prevalence, Tumor Spectrum, and Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Like Phenotype of CDKN2A-Related Melanoma-Astrocytoma Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (2 of 14, 14%) were the most common neural cancers

nodes.description: Full-skin dermatologic examination for melanoma every six months with monthly self-skin examinations, as for other CDKN2A melanoma-prone families.

evidence.reference_title: CDKN2A Cancer Predisposition.
evidence.snippet: Dermatologic examination for melanoma every six months; monthly self-skin examinations

nodes.description: Beyond astrocytic tumors, other nervous-system neoplasms including peripheral nerve sheath tumors and meningiomas occur in some families, consistent with the "neural system tumor" component of the syndrome name.

evidence.reference_title: Familial melanoma-astrocytoma syndrome: synchronous diffuse astrocytoma and pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma in a patient with germline CDKN2A/B deletion and a significant family history.
evidence.snippet: other families develop both melanomas, astrocytomas, and occasionally other nervous-system neoplasms including peripheral nerve sheath tumors and meningiomas.

nodes.description: Hyperphosphorylated RB releases E2F, driving the G1-to-S transition and cell-cycle entry independent of normal mitogenic control.

evidence.reference_title: The p16INK4a-RB pathway: molecular link between cellular senescence and tumor suppression.
evidence.snippet: Thus, p16INK4a has the capacity to arrest cells in the G1-phase of the cell cycle and its probable physiological role is in the implementation of irreversible growth arrest termed cellular senescence.

nodes.description: Schwannomas are among the most common benign neural tumors in ascertained cases.

evidence.reference_title: Estimated Prevalence, Tumor Spectrum, and Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Like Phenotype of CDKN2A-Related Melanoma-Astrocytoma Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: brain neoplasms (4 of 12, 33%; 1 glioblastoma, 1 gliosarcoma, 1 astrocytoma, 1 unspecified type) and schwannomas (3 of 12, 25%) were the most common malignant and benign neural tumors

nodes.description: In the tumor, the remaining wild-type 9p allele is lost somatically, producing biallelic CDKN2A inactivation. In melanoma-astrocytoma tumors this is seen as homozygous deletion of CDKN2A/B through loss of the other copy of chromosome 9p, completing the two-hit inactivation of both the p16INK4A and p14ARF arms.

evidence.reference_title: Familial melanoma-astrocytoma syndrome: synchronous diffuse astrocytoma and pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma in a patient with germline CDKN2A/B deletion and a significant family history.
evidence.snippet: Both the pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma and diffuse astrocytoma were found to have homozygous deletion of <italic>CDKN2A/B</italic> due to somatic loss of the other copy of chromosome 9p containing the remaining intact alleles.

evidence.reference_title: Germline mutation of ARF in a melanoma kindred.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of the melanoma from one individual revealed a 62 bp deletion in exon 3 of the wildtype allele and loss of the mutant allele; these somatic changes would affect both CDKN2A and ARF.

genetic_context.description: Somatic loss of the wild-type CDKN2A/B allele (loss of heterozygosity or homozygous deletion) on top of the germline lesion.

nodes.description: Ultraviolet exposure is the principal environmental modifier of melanoma penetrance in CDKN2A carriers, which is why sun protection and tanning-bed avoidance are part of management.

evidence.reference_title: Melanoma genetics: a review of genetic factors and clinical phenotypes in familial melanoma.
evidence.snippet: The penetrance of these melanoma-predisposing genes is largely influenced by ultraviolet exposure across geographic latitude.

nodes.description: Without p16INK4A, CDK4/6-cyclin D complexes are constitutively active and phosphorylate the retinoblastoma protein.

evidence.reference_title: The p16INK4a-RB pathway: molecular link between cellular senescence and tumor suppression.
evidence.snippet: The p16INK4a tumor suppressor protein functions as an inhibitor of CDK4 and CDK6, the D-type cyclin-dependent kinases that initiate the phosphorylation of the retinoblastoma tumor suppressor protein, RB.
